newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuke resumes ramp-up.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuke resumes ramp-up.

text.p: The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona has resumed ramping up to full power after being held at 32 percent Tuesday night due to a turbine vibration problem, a spokesman for Arizona Public Service Co said Wednesday.
He said the vibration problem was not a major issue and the unit will continue to ascend to various levels for further testing.
No estimate was given for when the unit, which was shut in late February for scheduled refueling, would reach 100 percent capacity.

The Palo Verde plant is jointly owned by Arizona Public Service Co, Salt River Project, Southern California Edison Co, El Paso Electric Co, Public Service Co of New Mexico, Southern California Public Power Authority and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.
